Package com.nexuslink.protocol.snmp

Class Oid

java.lang.Object
com.nexuslink.protocol.snmp.Oid
All Implemented Interfaces:
Comparable<Oid>
public final class Oid extends Object implements Comparable<Oid>
An immutable numeric SNMP object identifier: an ordered sequence of non-negative sub-identifiers such as 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.1.0. This is the value type behind the numeric-OID arithmetic that SNMP walking (GETNEXT) needs — lexicographic ordering, prefix tests and successor computation — complementing OidRegistry, which handles symbolic name resolution.

Everything here is pure, dependency-free and side-effect free: instances are deeply immutable (the backing array is never exposed) and safe to share across threads. Sub-identifiers are stored as long because SNMP allows values up to 232-1, which does not fit an int.

Ordering. compareTo(com.nexuslink.protocol.snmp.Oid) is the SNMP lexicographic order: compare sub-identifier by sub-identifier from the left; the first differing position decides, and if one OID is a strict prefix of the other the shorter one sorts first. So 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.1 < 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.1.0 < 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.2.

Successor. next() returns this OID with a trailing .0 appended. That is the conventional "just past this node" bound used to seed a GETNEXT walk: for any OID x, x < x.next() and there is no OID strictly between them that is not itself a descendant of x, so starting a walk at x.next() enumerates the whole subtree rooted at x.

  • Field Details

    • MAX_SUB_ID

      public static final long MAX_SUB_ID
      Largest legal sub-identifier: SNMP sub-identifiers are unsigned 32-bit (2^32 - 1).
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

  • Method Details

    • parse

      public static Oid parse(String text)
      Parses a dotted OID such as "1.3.6.1.2.1.1.1.0" into an Oid. A single optional leading dot is accepted (".1.3.6" parses the same as "1.3.6"). Every component must be a non-negative decimal integer no larger than MAX_SUB_ID.
      Throws:
      OidFormatException - if text is null, blank, has an empty component (e.g. "1..2" or a trailing dot), or a component that is negative, non-numeric or out of range.

    • of

      public static Oid of(long... subIds)
      Builds an Oid directly from sub-identifiers. Each must be in [0, MAX_SUB_ID] and at least one must be supplied.
      Throws:
      OidFormatException - if no sub-identifiers are given or any is out of range.

    • length

      public int length()
      The number of sub-identifiers in this OID (always at least one).

    • get

      public long get(int index)
      The sub-identifier at index (0-based, left to right).
      Throws:
      IndexOutOfBoundsException - if index is outside [0, length()).

    • toList

      public List<Long> toList()
      An immutable List view of the sub-identifiers, in order.

    • sub

      public Oid sub(int from, int to)
      A new OID consisting of sub-identifiers [from, to). Semantics mirror List.subList(int, int).
      Throws:
      IndexOutOfBoundsException - if the range is invalid.
      OidFormatException - if the range is empty (an OID needs at least one sub-identifier).

    • child

      public Oid child(long... more)
      A new OID with more appended to this one, e.g. Oid.parse("1.3.6").child(1, 0) is 1.3.6.1.0. Calling with no arguments returns this OID unchanged.
      Throws:
      OidFormatException - if any appended sub-identifier is out of [0, MAX_SUB_ID].

    • parent

      public Oid parent()
      This OID with its last sub-identifier removed, e.g. the parent of 1.3.6.1 is 1.3.6. A single-component OID has no parent.
      Throws:
      OidFormatException - if this OID has only one sub-identifier.

    • isPrefixOf

      public boolean isPrefixOf(Oid other)
      True when this OID is a prefix of other — i.e. other is this node or a descendant of it. An OID is a prefix of itself. Used by a walk to detect when GETNEXT has stepped outside the requested subtree.

    • startsWith

      public boolean startsWith(Oid prefix)
      The mirror of isPrefixOf(com.nexuslink.protocol.snmp.Oid): true when prefix is a prefix of this OID.

    • next

      public Oid next()
      The conventional GETNEXT successor: this OID with a trailing .0 appended. See the class documentation for why this seeds a subtree walk. x.next() is always strictly greater than x under compareTo(com.nexuslink.protocol.snmp.Oid).
